![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14222477/assets/8934e5b6135b97b845dad9a6b87056d2c228fd2424d3a72141df694d46ccf7c0.png)

Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate the parabola shown above?
question.worked_solution:
The diagram shows that the parabola is vertical, has its vertex at $(0,0),$ and passes through the point $(-6,12).$

The parametric equations of a vertical parabola  that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ are

$$
x=2pt,\,y=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

Since the parabola passes through $(-6,12),$ we can substitute $x=-6$ and $y=12$ into the standard parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-6=2pt \\ 12=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-6 & =2pt \\ -3 & =pt \\ t & =-\frac{3}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =p{(-\frac{3}{p})}^{2} \\ 12 & =p\cdot \frac{9}{{p}^{2}} \\ 12 & =\frac{9}{p} \\ p & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x=2(\frac{3}{4})t,\,y=(\frac{3}{4}){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x=\frac{3}{2}t,\,y=\frac{3}{4}{t}^{2}.
$$
